subject: Cardinal AI — DPA / No‑Train Commitment and Onshore Cutover Plan
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cardinalai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalai.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Nov 2027 14:02:00 -0500
Subject: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)

Neha — thanks again for the quick demo last week. Procurement has a few blocking asks before we can sign the SOW and DPA: 

1) A written, contract-level "no training / no model improvement" commitment for data sent via API (we need explicit language we can present to our legal team).
2) Onshore data residency for logs/exports during the pilot (Cardinal requires SFTP to an onshore bucket and confirmation that any KMS for key material remains within the US).
3) Full list of subprocessors that will touch prompt/response data, plus an attestation they won't use data for product training.

I've attached our procurement SLA and a checklist of regulatory items for the pilot. Can you send a redline or sample clause we can take to our counsel? Also: what's the timeline to stand up an onshore SFTP endpoint and Ops contact for the integration?

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform Engineering, Cardinal AI
Attachment: Cardinal_Procurement_SLA.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cardinalai.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)

Alex — appreciate the clear list. Quick summary / next steps from our side: 

- We can commit contractually to a "no training / no model improvement" clause scoped to Customer Data (prompts and responses) for the duration of the agreed term and pilot. I attached a redline DPA (redline-dpa-neha-v1.pdf) with suggested wording; David (Legal) added some optional language for derivative notices.
- Onshore SFTP: Ops can provision an SFTP landing zone in our US region for the pilot. Connor will coordinate the handshake (SFTP creds + host key exchange).
- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration; if you require Redwood to use an onshore KMS instance or restrict key wrapping to the US, we can document the specific constraints in the DPA addendum.
- Subprocessors: we'll provide the current list and an attestation. We cannot guarantee there will be zero subprocessors, but we will commit that none will use data for model improvement and will include that in the subprocessor addendum.

Proposed timeline:
- Tue 16 Nov: Ops handshake call (30 min) to scope SFTP and sample payloads
- Wed 17 Nov: Legal to review/redline the DPA clause; finalize DocuSign envelope if acceptable
- Mon 22 Nov: Pilot cutover window (assuming paperwork signed)

I'll loop David for the exact clause text below. If that timeline works, I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
Attachment: redline-dpa-neha-v1.pdf
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cardinalai.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)

Alex / Neha — sending proposed contract language below that we included in the redline: feel free to copy into your counsel's template. We're happy to negotiate exact scope, but this is the starting point we can sign to for the pilot period.

--- PROPOSED CLAUSE (copyable) ---
"No Model Training. Redwood Inference shall not use, incorporate, or otherwise exploit Customer Data (including prompts, responses, or metadata) to train, fine-tune, or improve any machine learning models, model weights, or model-serving pipelines. For the avoidance of doubt, Redwood will not run offline or online training jobs that consume Customer Data, and will not use Customer Data to augment datasets used for model research, benchmarking, or product improvements. This restriction applies to Redwood and its subprocessors for the duration of the Agreement, unless otherwise agreed in writing.\n"

Other operational notes:
- Retention: we'll document retention periods for logs and the SFTP export in the DPA addendum (default pilot retention: 30 days unless otherwise specified).
- Evidence: we can provide an attestation of subprocessor obligations and a TLS+host-key fingerprint for the SFTP endpoint.
- Export controls: please confirm whether Cardinal needs export-control restrictions beyond US-only storage (e.g., prohibiting cross-border backups).

If you want a further narrowing (for example, exclude aggregated telemetry or metrics from the clause), say so and we can add an exception.

-David
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
From: Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cardinalai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalai.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 08:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)

David / Neha — that proposed clause is helpful and closer to what counsel needs. A couple of procurement clarifications: 

- We need to see the live subprocessor list (not just a commitment) and a separate signed attestation that subprocessors will not use data for model training. Can you provide the current list and the attestation PDF?
- For KMS: Cardinal's security policy requires the key material to remain within a US border and for any KMS operations that wrap/unwrap keys to occur on-prem or in an approved US-based HSM. Can Redwood accept a recorded covenant that key material will not be exported?
- Pricing: if onshore SFTP+reserved onshore capacity requires a dedicated pool, procurement needs a delta against the quoted hosted price. Please have sales (Marissa) provide a delta table.

Also — confirming Ops call Tues at 16:00 ET (Connor, you'll get a calendar invite).

Alex
Attachment: Cardinal_Questions_Procurement.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Procurement Team <procurement@cardinalai.com>, Alex Mercer <alex.mercer@cardinalai.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Nov 2027 11:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)

Hi Alex / Procurement — quick note from sales on the pricing ask: 

- Dedicated US onshore capacity (reserved pool) + SFTP onboarding is estimated at an additional $3,500/month on top of the hosted rates for the pilot profile you shared. That includes a small ops onboarding fee and reserved capacity to meet the latency/throughput SLAs you requested.
- If Cardinal signs a 12-month committed contract we can offer a 10% discount on the dedicated capacity line.

Next steps we propose: 
1) Finalize DPA redlines this week (David / Neha)
2) DocuSign envelope with DPA + SOW (we'll prepare and share)
3) Ops handshake + SFTP exchange (Connor owns)
4) Pilot cutover once DocuSign complete and SFTP test passed

I've attached a draft SOW with the pricing table. If procurement needs a formal quote, we'll issue it from the finance portal.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW-draft-Cardinal.pdf
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: DPA + no-train commitment questions (Cardinal AI)
